**The start date: 1 January 2028 — not this year.**

The 28 September 2025 vote approved the reform, but it takes effect on 1 January 2028 (the Federal Council set the date to give cantons time to adapt; Zurich applies it on the same date). So your 2025, 2026 and 2027 tax returns are unchanged — you keep declaring Eigenmietwert. The first tax year without it is 2028, assessed in 2029.

**What to do:**

- **Keep amortising until 2027.** Nothing changes, and your mortgage contract almost certainly obliges you to anyway (banks require the loan amortised down to 2/3 of the property value within 15 years — you can't unilaterally stop).
- **Don't assume abolition means "keep the debt forever."** The reform comes with payback measures: mortgage interest will only be deductible for a limited period (new purchases: 10 years; existing loans: transitional rules — roughly a 10-year window from 2028), and maintenance deductions become capped lump sums. Holding a big mortgage loses most of its tax logic, so amortising actually becomes *more* attractive for most owners — and it cuts Zurich wealth tax too.
- **If you want more flexibility:** ask your bank about switching from direct to indirect amortisation via pillar 3a — those contributions stay tax-deductible.
- **Simple rule:** from 2028, only keep debt if your investments clearly beat your mortgage rate after tax.

One caveat: the transitional rules for existing mortgages are still being finalised, so confirm your specific case with the bank before changing anything.
